rows.statement: The first intercollegiate football game was played on 6 November 1869 in New Brunswick, New Jersey (Rutgers 6, Princeton 4). The world's past may start no earlier than this season.

sources.citation: Rutgers University, 'In the first collegiate football game 150 years ago, Rutgers beat Princeton' (David W. Major, 2019-11-06)
sources.quote: to play the first collegiate football game, on November 6, 1869.

sources.citation: Princeton Alumni Weekly, 'Chronicling Football's First Games' (Brett Tomlinson, 2019-11-04; reprint of Parke H. Davis, 1909)
sources.quote: The contest was between Princeton and Rutgers at New Brunswick, November 6, 1869.

sources.citation: History.com, 'Rutgers beats Princeton in the first college football game' (History.com Staff, updated 2025-05-27)
sources.quote: On November 6, 1869, Rutgers beats Princeton, 6-4, in the first college football game.

sources.citation: Rutgers Athletics archive, 'The First Game: Nov. 6, 1869'
sources.quote: played the first game of intercollegiate football on Nov. 6, 1869.

rows.notes: Four pages read 2026-11-26 by fetch; Sports Illustrated (Patrick Andres, 2025-08-28) also agrees on Nov. 6 in New Brunswick. The rutgers.edu and scarletknights.com pages share one independence group. Real teams are calibration only; world teams are fictional.

statusHistory.reason: Two primary institutional sources (Rutgers, Princeton) plus History.com agree.
